policies.title: Leadership commitment and safety responsibilities
policies.description: The company supports safe work by providing suitable equipment, understandable instructions and time to address hazards. This policy applies to company operations and the people directing them.
policies.policyText:
# Leadership commitment and safety responsibilities

The company supports safe work by providing suitable equipment, understandable instructions and time to address hazards. This policy applies to company operations and the people directing them.

Managers make safety responsibilities clear when allocating work. Supervisors explain the task, arrange the people and equipment needed to perform it safely, and respond to concerns raised by workers. Workers follow the safety instructions relevant to their work and tell their supervisor when conditions or equipment make those instructions unsafe or impractical.

Production targets do not justify exposing people to an uncontrolled serious hazard. When a concern cannot be resolved at the work area, the supervisor brings it to the manager able to provide a solution. Work affected by the hazard remains stopped while that solution is put in place.

Management uses information from workers, incidents and equipment problems to correct conditions that could cause harm. Raising a safety concern or reporting an injury in good faith does not result in retaliation.

policies.title: Worker participation and safety communication
policies.description: Workers have direct knowledge of the work and a voice in how it is performed safely. This policy applies to safety communication within the company, including conversations between workers, supervisors and managers.
policies.policyText:
# Worker participation and safety communication

Workers have direct knowledge of the work and a voice in how it is performed safely. This policy applies to safety communication within the company, including conversations between workers, supervisors and managers.

Supervisors explain hazards and changes in language workers understand, invite questions, and give workers an opportunity to describe problems with the task. Workers can raise concerns directly with their supervisor or another manager when the supervisor is unavailable or involved in the concern. Reports are considered on their facts; good-faith reporting does not result in retaliation.

Safety discussions address the actual work: what could hurt someone, what prevents that harm, and what has changed. A conversation at the work area can address a simple issue; a wider discussion can address a change affecting several crews.

The supervisor communicates the resolution to the people affected. If an immediate hazard remains, the affected work is paused rather than waiting for a meeting.

policies.title: Stop work and safe restart
policies.description: Anyone who identifies an immediate danger can stop the affected activity and move to a safe position. This policy applies to company work and to hazards created by work taking place nearby.
policies.policyText:
# Stop work and safe restart

Anyone who identifies an immediate danger can stop the affected activity and move to a safe position. This policy applies to company work and to hazards created by work taking place nearby.

The person raising the concern tells the people exposed and the supervisor what was observed. The supervisor makes the area safe, listens to the concern, and addresses the condition with the people who understand the equipment or activity. A stop should cover the work exposed to the hazard; unrelated work can continue when it remains safe.

Work restarts after the hazard has been removed or controlled and the affected people understand the safe method. Where the activity has an applicable legal permit, isolation or entry condition, that condition is restored before the activity resumes. A supervisor does not direct a worker to bypass a safeguard to recover lost time.

No one is penalized for a good-faith stop or for reporting a hazard. If the parties disagree about safety, the matter goes to a manager who can resolve the hazard before the affected work proceeds.

policies.title: Subcontractor selection and safety coordination
policies.description: The company selects subcontractors for the work they will actually perform and coordinates shared hazards before that work begins. This policy applies when the company engages another business to perform part of its service.
policies.policyText:
# Subcontractor selection and safety coordination

The company selects subcontractors for the work they will actually perform and coordinates shared hazards before that work begins. This policy applies when the company engages another business to perform part of its service.

The person arranging the subcontract explains the scope, location and hazards known to the company. The subcontractor explains its work method and any hazards it may introduce to other people. Together they identify who controls shared equipment, isolations, access and emergency communication. A short discussion can resolve a straightforward interface.

The subcontractor provides people and equipment suitable for its agreed work. When a specialist license or qualification is legally required for that work, the selection takes that requirement into account. A change in scope is discussed before the added activity exposes people to new hazards.

If work creates an uncontrolled danger, the affected activity stops while the companies resolve it. For work on a process actually covered by OSHA process safety management, the host and contract employers also perform their respective contractor duties under that regulation.

policies.title: Service scope, legal duties and current instructions
policies.description: Safety requirements follow the services the company performs, the work location and the hazards people encounter. This policy applies when selecting services, planning work or issuing instructions.
policies.policyText:
# Service scope, legal duties and current instructions

Safety requirements follow the services the company performs, the work location and the hazards people encounter. This policy applies when selecting services, planning work or issuing instructions.

Managers describe the company's services accurately. Supervisors use instructions suited to the task and equipment in use. Workers ask for clarification when instructions conflict, are unreadable or describe a different task. An outdated instruction is replaced or corrected before it leads someone into an unsafe action.

Legal requirements are applied to the activity and jurisdiction that trigger them. A requirement for one kind of operation is not automatically imposed on every company, role or service. Company staff can obtain the current instructions and safety information needed for their work.

When a service, piece of equipment or work method changes, the supervisor checks whether the existing instructions still address its hazards. Conflicts affecting safety are resolved with the responsible company or site contact before the affected work continues.

policies.title: Task hazard assessment
policies.description: Work is planned with attention to the hazards of the actual task, its surroundings and other people who may be affected. This policy applies to routine work, unfamiliar tasks and changes during work.
policies.policyText:
# Task hazard assessment

Work is planned with attention to the hazards of the actual task, its surroundings and other people who may be affected. This policy applies to routine work, unfamiliar tasks and changes during work.

Before starting, the people doing the work consider the main steps, sources of energy, movements, substances and environmental conditions that could cause harm. They choose controls that remove the hazard where practicable, then use suitable equipment, separation, work methods and protective equipment for remaining exposure. The supervisor resolves hazards the crew cannot control itself.

A familiar low-risk task may be addressed through a brief conversation and existing instructions. A written job hazard analysis is used when an applicable requirement calls for it or the company chooses it for the task;

Workers pause when the scope, equipment, people or conditions change in a way that defeats the planned controls. They adjust the method with the supervisor before resuming. If a safeguard cannot be established, the affected activity does not proceed.

policies.title: Line of fire and critical safeguards
policies.description: People are kept clear of paths in which moving equipment, suspended material, pressure or stored energy could injure them. This policy applies wherever a person could be struck, crushed, caught or exposed to a sudden release.
policies.policyText:
# Line of fire and critical safeguards

People are kept clear of paths in which moving equipment, suspended material, pressure or stored energy could injure them. This policy applies wherever a person could be struck, crushed, caught or exposed to a sudden release.

The crew identifies the likely direction of movement or release before positioning people. Equipment is stabilized, loads restrained and guards or barriers used for the hazard involved. Hands and bodies stay out of pinch points. A spotter stands where the operator can see them and where movement cannot trap them. People do not rely on eye contact alone when a physical separation is needed.

The operator confirms that the work area is clear before movement begins. Workers do not enter a guarded or isolated area while hazardous motion or energy remains. If a barrier is moved, a restraint fails or the operator loses sight of someone exposed, the affected movement stops.

The supervisor and crew restore the safeguard or choose another safe method before continuing. Checking a safeguard means confirming the physical condition, not merely checking a box.

policies.title: Permit-to-work and simultaneous operations
policies.description: Activities that can affect one another are coordinated so one crew does not defeat another crew's safeguards. This policy applies to overlapping work and to tasks subject to a legal or applicable site permit system.
policies.policyText:
# Permit-to-work and simultaneous operations

Activities that can affect one another are coordinated so one crew does not defeat another crew's safeguards. This policy applies to overlapping work and to tasks subject to a legal or applicable site permit system.

The supervisor identifies nearby activities, shared equipment and boundaries that could change the task's safety. Crews agree the timing, separation and communication needed for those interfaces. For permitted work, the people issuing and performing the work confirm the scope, location, hazards and required precautions before starting. A permit records the arrangement; the actual isolation, ventilation, fire precautions or barriers must also be in place.

Workers stay within the agreed scope and communicate changes. If another activity introduces a hazard, or a permit condition is no longer met, the affected work pauses while the crews resolve the conflict. Work resumes within the applicable permit conditions and safe arrangement.

At handback, the crew tells the person controlling the equipment what work is complete and what condition remains.

policies.title: Control of hazardous energy
policies.description: Equipment is protected against unexpected startup, movement and release of stored energy during servicing that exposes people to those hazards. The supervisor selects the energy-control method applicable to the equipment and activity.
policies.policyText:
# Control of hazardous energy

Equipment is protected against unexpected startup, movement and release of stored energy during servicing that exposes people to those hazards. The supervisor selects the energy-control method applicable to the equipment and activity.

The worker performing isolation identifies all energy sources, shuts equipment down, isolates the sources and applies the required lockout or tagout devices. Stored pressure, gravity, electrical charge and other residual energy are released, restrained or otherwise controlled. Isolation is verified before exposure begins. A stop button or control selector alone is not an energy-isolating device.

Each person covered by a group isolation receives protection through the applicable group procedure. Shift changes and contractor interfaces maintain continuous protection. Workers do not remove another person's device except through the exceptional-removal procedure permitted by the governing energy-control standard.

Before restoration, equipment is checked, people are clear and affected workers are informed. Where 29 CFR 1910.147 applies, its written procedures, role-specific training and at-least-annual procedure inspections apply, subject to the standard's stated exceptions. Those duties are limited to work within that standard's scope.

policies.title: Confined-space entry
policies.description: The company identifies spaces with restricted entry or exit and evaluates the hazards before people enter them. Employees do not enter a space simply because it appears empty or because someone else entered it previously.
policies.policyText:
# Confined-space entry

The company identifies spaces with restricted entry or exit and evaluates the hazards before people enter them. Employees do not enter a space simply because it appears empty or because someone else entered it previously.

For a permit-required space, the employer uses the entry program and permit required by the applicable confined-space standard. The entry arrangement addresses isolation, atmospheric testing, ventilation, communication, the attendant's duties and rescue. Entrants understand the hazards and leave when an alarm, prohibited condition or instruction to evacuate occurs. Entry supervisors confirm entry conditions and end entry when those conditions fail.

Atmospheric testing uses suitable equipment and considers oxygen, flammable atmospheres and toxic contaminants. Ventilation does not replace isolation of sources that could engulf, energize or contaminate the space. Rescue is arranged before entry; an unprotected coworker does not enter to attempt an improvised rescue.

General-industry permit entries follow 29 CFR 1910.146, including required training and rescue provisions. Construction entries follow the construction confined-space rules. Alternative procedures or reclassification are used only when their regulatory conditions are met.

policies.title: Hot work and fire prevention
policies.description: Welding, cutting and other ignition-producing work are performed where sparks, hot material and flame cannot ignite combustible material or a hazardous atmosphere. This policy applies to hot work in shops and at field locations.
policies.policyText:
# Hot work and fire prevention

Welding, cutting and other ignition-producing work are performed where sparks, hot material and flame cannot ignite combustible material or a hazardous atmosphere. This policy applies to hot work in shops and at field locations.

The worker checks the surrounding area, including openings and the opposite side of walls or floors. Combustible material is moved away or protected. Containers and equipment that held flammable material are prepared for hot work before cutting or welding begins. Cylinders, hoses and electrical leads are kept in safe condition and positioned away from damage.

The person responsible for the area authorizes hot work under the applicable arrangement. A fire watch is provided where the conditions in the governing welding and cutting standard require one, with suitable extinguishing equipment and the required watch period. Hot-work permits are used where a governing rule or the site's permit system requires them.

Work stops if flammable vapors, uncontrolled sparks or changing conditions defeat fire precautions. Anyone discovering a fire raises the alarm, withdraws as needed and calls for help rather than attempting an unsafe firefighting action.

policies.title: Lifting, rigging and suspended loads
policies.description: Lifting equipment and rigging are selected and used within their capacity for the actual load and arrangement. This policy applies to cranes, hoists and rigged loads.
policies.policyText:
# Lifting, rigging and suspended loads

Lifting equipment and rigging are selected and used within their capacity for the actual load and arrangement. This policy applies to cranes, hoists and rigged loads.

The people planning the lift establish the load's weight, balance, attachment points and intended path. Rigging is suitable for the load, hitch and working conditions. Damaged or unidentified gear is not used where its capacity or condition cannot be established. The operator considers equipment configuration, ground support and obstructions before lifting.

People remain outside the fall and crush path of a load. No one rides a suspended load or passes beneath it. The operator follows the agreed signals and stops if a signal is unclear or the load moves unexpectedly. Tag lines are used only where they can be handled without putting a person in the load path or creating an entanglement hazard.

Crane operators, riggers and signal persons meet the requirements applicable to their equipment and work. Construction crane certification and signal-person qualification are applied where the construction crane standard requires them, rather than to every worker near a lift.

policies.title: Work at height and dropped objects
policies.description: Elevated work is arranged to prevent falls and protect people below. This policy applies to work near unprotected edges, openings, scaffolds and other elevated positions.
policies.policyText:
# Work at height and dropped objects

Elevated work is arranged to prevent falls and protect people below. This policy applies to work near unprotected edges, openings, scaffolds and other elevated positions.

The supervisor selects safe access and a working surface suitable for the task. Guardrails, covers or other collective protection are used where appropriate. When personal fall protection is required, the system is suitable for the anchorage, fall distance and equipment involved. Workers inspect their equipment and keep connectors, harnesses and lifelines away from damaging edges and incompatible connections.

Ladders are placed on a stable surface, secured where needed and used without overreaching. Scaffolds are erected, inspected and used under the applicable scaffold rules. Tools and materials are kept from falling by secure storage, toe boards, tool retention or separation of the area below, as suited to the work.

Work stops when access, edge protection or fall protection becomes unsafe. Fall-height thresholds, training and rescue duties follow the standard governing the activity; construction and general-industry thresholds are not treated as interchangeable.

policies.title: Excavation and buried services
policies.description: Excavation is planned to prevent cave-ins, strikes on buried services and falls into the work area. This policy applies to digging, trenching and ground disturbance.
policies.policyText:
# Excavation and buried services

Excavation is planned to prevent cave-ins, strikes on buried services and falls into the work area. This policy applies to digging, trenching and ground disturbance.

Before excavation, the responsible person locates underground utilities using the required locating process and establishes their position as the work approaches them. Equipment, spoil and traffic are positioned so they do not undermine the edge or expose people to falling material. Workers stay clear of excavation equipment and suspended loads.

For construction excavations, the competent person performs the inspections required by 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P, including daily inspections before work and after conditions that increase the hazard. Protective systems, access and egress, atmospheric precautions and water controls are provided when the standard's conditions trigger them. Employees do not enter an excavation showing signs of failure while those conditions remain.

If a utility is damaged, soil moves, water enters or an atmospheric hazard develops, people leave the affected area and notify the supervisor. Work resumes only after the hazard has been addressed. Depth alone does not establish that a trench is safe.

policies.title: Pressure pumping and testing
policies.description: Pressure operations are arranged to prevent injury from released fluid, failed components and moving pipe or hose. This policy applies to pressure pumping, pressure testing and similar work.
policies.policyText:
# Pressure pumping and testing

Pressure operations are arranged to prevent injury from released fluid, failed components and moving pipe or hose. This policy applies to pressure pumping, pressure testing and similar work.

The person directing the operation establishes the intended pressure, test medium and equipment limits. Components and connections are compatible with those conditions. Relief devices and pressure indications are suitable for the system. People are positioned away from likely release paths, unsupported components and connections that could whip or separate.

Pressure is increased in a controlled manner while the operator watches for leaks, movement and abnormal indications. No one tightens, disconnects or repairs a pressurized connection. A leak is not located by placing a hand in the release path. The system is depressurized and its safe condition confirmed before adjustment or opening.

If equipment moves, pressure behaves unexpectedly or containment fails, the operator stops and releases pressure safely. Access remains restricted until the danger is controlled. Specific test procedures and equipment limits come from the actual system and governing equipment requirements, not a universal pressure value or fixed exclusion distance.

policies.title: Opening process equipment and handback
policies.description: Piping, vessels and other process equipment are opened only after their contents and stored energy have been controlled. This policy applies to disconnecting, draining, opening or removing components that may contain pressure or hazardous material.
policies.policyText:
# Opening process equipment and handback

Piping, vessels and other process equipment are opened only after their contents and stored energy have been controlled. This policy applies to disconnecting, draining, opening or removing components that may contain pressure or hazardous material.

The crew identifies the correct equipment and communicates with the person controlling the process. Isolation addresses all connected sources. Pressure is relieved, contents managed and residual hazards checked before the first opening. Workers use a position and method that keep them clear of a possible release, with protective equipment suited to the material.

An unexpected pressure indication, blocked drain, leak or unidentified connection is treated as a reason to pause and resolve the condition. Loosening a connection is not used as the initial means of proving equipment depressurized when a safer verification method is available.

After work, the crew tells the process controller which components were changed, what remains open or isolated, and whether the equipment is ready for restoration. Restoration follows the applicable isolation and operating procedure. The area is checked for leaks and exposed people are clear before the process returns to service.

policies.title: Electrical safety
policies.description: Electrical work protects people from shock, burns and unexpected equipment operation. This policy applies to electrical equipment and work near exposed electrical hazards.
policies.policyText:
# Electrical safety

Electrical work protects people from shock, burns and unexpected equipment operation. This policy applies to electrical equipment and work near exposed electrical hazards.

Workers keep enclosures closed, use equipment suited to its location and report damaged leads, exposed conductors or overheating. Damaged equipment is disconnected or removed from use without exposing the person doing so. Non-electrical workers keep clear of exposed energized parts and overhead lines.

Electrical work is deenergized where required by the governing standard. The worker performing the work isolates the supply, controls stored energy and verifies the deenergized condition using suitable test equipment. Electrical qualification is specific to the task. Where energized work is legally permitted, qualified workers use the work practices, approach protection and protective equipment required for the exposure.

Only people performing the relevant electrical task receive the duties of a qualified electrical worker; an awareness course does not make every employee an electrician. If a person receives an electrical shock, others isolate the source before touching them and summon emergency help. Work does not resume with damaged insulation or an unresolved electrical fault.

policies.title: Hydrogen sulfide and hazardous atmospheres
policies.description: Work in areas that may contain hydrogen sulfide or another dangerous atmosphere is planned around exposure prevention, detection and escape. This policy applies to affected production, tank, monitoring and support work.
policies.policyText:
# Hydrogen sulfide and hazardous atmospheres

Work in areas that may contain hydrogen sulfide or another dangerous atmosphere is planned around exposure prevention, detection and escape. This policy applies to affected production, tank, monitoring and support work.

The supervisor identifies likely release sources and communicates alarms, escape routes and assembly points. Where monitoring is needed, the crew uses a detector suitable for the gases and conditions, checks its readiness and keeps it where it can detect the exposure. Smell is not used to judge whether hydrogen sulfide is present or whether an area is safe.

An alarm or signs of a release prompt withdrawal to a safe location, avoiding the release path and low areas. People notify others who may be exposed and contact the site's emergency response. They do not reenter to investigate or rescue without the protection and response capability appropriate to the atmosphere.

Respirator use follows the respiratory-protection requirements triggered by the task. Unknown or immediately dangerous atmospheres are not treated as ordinary nuisance exposures. Workers report a detector fault or a missing escape route before continuing exposed work.

policies.title: Chemical information and exposure control
policies.description: People receive the information and protection needed to use hazardous chemicals safely. This policy applies to chemicals brought into, stored or used in company work.
policies.policyText:
# Chemical information and exposure control

People receive the information and protection needed to use hazardous chemicals safely. This policy applies to chemicals brought into, stored or used in company work.

The company maintains the hazard-communication program required for its hazardous chemicals, including labels, accessible safety data sheets and employee information and training. Workers read the product label and relevant instructions before use and keep containers identified. Chemicals are stored so incompatible substances do not mix and containers are protected from damage.

The supervisor considers how the chemical is used, including mist, vapor, dust and skin contact. Substitution, containment and ventilation are used as appropriate before relying on personal protection alone. Workers use the correct protective equipment and keep food and drink away from contaminated areas.

A spill, unexpected reaction or exposure is reported promptly. Workers leave a dangerous area and obtain emergency help when needed. They do not mix chemicals or improvise cleanup with an incompatible product. Where exposure monitoring or medical surveillance is required by a substance-specific standard, it applies to the affected work and employees.

policies.title: Respiratory protection
policies.description: Respirators are selected for the contaminant, concentration and work conditions when engineering or other controls do not adequately protect employees. Required respirator use is managed under the applicable respiratory-protection program.
policies.policyText:
# Respiratory protection

Respirators are selected for the contaminant, concentration and work conditions when engineering or other controls do not adequately protect employees. Required respirator use is managed under the applicable respiratory-protection program.

For work covered by 29 CFR 1910.134, the employer provides a suitable written program and a qualified program administrator. Required users receive a medical evaluation before fit testing or use. Tight-fitting respirators are fit tested before initial use, when the facepiece changes and at least annually, with additional testing when physical changes could affect fit. Users receive the required training and inspect and care for the respirator.

Workers perform a user seal check each time a tight-fitting respirator is put on. Facial hair or other conditions must not interfere with its seal or valve function. Cartridges follow the selected change schedule or appropriate service-life indicator, rather than odor alone.

If breathing resistance, leakage or equipment failure occurs, the worker leaves the hazardous area before removing the respirator. Voluntary use is handled under the standard's voluntary-use provisions, including the filtering-facepiece exception; required-use duties are not automatically applied to every dust-mask user.

policies.title: Silica, asbestos, lead and coating exposure
policies.description: Work that can disturb hazardous dusts, fibers or coatings is identified before material is cut, blasted, demolished or removed. This policy applies to affected construction, maintenance, surface preparation and abatement tasks.
policies.policyText:
# Silica, asbestos, lead and coating exposure

Work that can disturb hazardous dusts, fibers or coatings is identified before material is cut, blasted, demolished or removed. This policy applies to affected construction, maintenance, surface preparation and abatement tasks.

The supervisor determines what material is present and how the task may expose people. Workers do not assume an older coating, insulation or building material is harmless because it looks familiar. The work method uses appropriate containment, dust collection, wet methods or other controls for the material and activity. Dry sweeping and compressed-air cleaning are avoided where prohibited or where they spread hazardous dust.

The employer applies the substance-specific standard that actually governs the work. Silica exposure-control plans, asbestos training and regulated areas, lead monitoring and medical surveillance are provided when the respective regulatory conditions require them. Required respirator use follows the respiratory-protection program.

Unexpected suspect material or failed dust control prompts a pause in the affected operation. Contaminated material is contained and handled without exposing nearby people or carrying contamination into eating areas, vehicles or homes. Material identification and exposure results determine the next safe method.

policies.title: Noise and hearing protection
policies.description: Noise exposure is controlled to protect hearing and preserve the ability to communicate warnings. This policy applies to noisy equipment and work areas.
policies.policyText:
# Noise and hearing protection

Noise exposure is controlled to protect hearing and preserve the ability to communicate warnings. This policy applies to noisy equipment and work areas.

The supervisor considers the level and duration of exposure and arranges measurement when needed to determine whether hearing-conservation duties apply. Quieter equipment, maintenance, isolation and other feasible controls are considered before relying only on hearing protectors. Workers wear the selected protection correctly in designated noisy work and tell the supervisor when it prevents essential communication or does not fit.

For employees covered by 29 CFR 1910.95, the hearing-conservation program applies at the standard's action level and includes the required monitoring, audiometry, protectors and training. Construction noise requirements are applied to construction work.

Workers report ringing, muffled hearing or a sudden change after noise exposure and obtain appropriate medical attention. A missing protector or unexpected increase in noise is addressed before exposure continues. Hearing protection is selected for the actual noise, not simply because it has the highest advertised rating.

policies.title: Heat, cold and severe weather
policies.description: Weather and temperature are considered when arranging outdoor work and physically demanding tasks. This policy applies to people exposed to heat, cold, lightning, wind or other severe weather.
policies.policyText:
# Heat, cold and severe weather

Weather and temperature are considered when arranging outdoor work and physically demanding tasks. This policy applies to people exposed to heat, cold, lightning, wind or other severe weather.

The supervisor considers workload, clothing, humidity, sun, wind and each worker's adjustment to the conditions. Drinking water, suitable rest opportunities and access to cooling or warming are arranged for the exposure. Work can be moved, rescheduled or reduced when conditions make the planned method unsafe. New or returning workers receive attention while adjusting to heat or cold.

Workers watch for illness in themselves and coworkers. Confusion, collapse or suspected heat stroke is an emergency: call for medical help and begin appropriate cooling without delaying the call. Cold-related loss of coordination, numbness or altered behavior also requires prompt action.

During lightning, high winds or flooding, crews leave exposed positions and use suitable shelter. Work resumes when the specific hazard has passed and the area is safe. Applicable state heat rules and task-specific weather limits are followed where they govern;

policies.title: Driving and fatigue
policies.description: Company driving is arranged so the driver can remain alert and operate the vehicle safely. This policy applies to travel performed for company work.
policies.policyText:
# Driving and fatigue

Company driving is arranged so the driver can remain alert and operate the vehicle safely. This policy applies to travel performed for company work.

Drivers use the correct license for the vehicle, wear seat belts, obey traffic laws and secure the vehicle's load. They check visibility, tires, lights and other conditions relevant to safe travel and report defects. Phones or other distractions are not used in a way that takes attention from driving. Speed is adjusted for traffic, road surface, weather and visibility rather than relying only on the posted limit.

The person arranging travel considers journey length, working time, rest and the availability of a safe stopping place. A fatigued driver stops in a safe location and tells the supervisor when the trip cannot be completed safely. Schedule pressure does not justify continuing while impaired or sleepy.

Regulated commercial driving follows the applicable hours-of-service, qualification and inspection rules. Those rules are not imposed on unrelated workers or vehicles outside their scope. After a collision or roadside breakdown, people protect themselves from traffic, call for help and avoid unsafe recovery attempts.

policies.title: Traffic, gate access and pedestrian safety
policies.description: Vehicle and pedestrian movements are arranged to avoid collisions and crushing. This policy applies to gates, yards, delivery areas and work around mobile equipment.
policies.policyText:
# Traffic, gate access and pedestrian safety

Vehicle and pedestrian movements are arranged to avoid collisions and crushing. This policy applies to gates, yards, delivery areas and work around mobile equipment.

Drivers follow the site's routes and traffic directions, approach gates at a controlled speed and stop where directed. Gate and yard staff stand outside vehicle paths and avoid positions between a vehicle and a fixed object. Pedestrians use separated routes where available and do not assume an operator can see them.

Before reversing or moving into a congested area, the driver confirms the route is clear. When a spotter is used, the driver and spotter agree the signals and stop if communication is lost. Barriers and warning devices are positioned so they guide traffic without creating a new obstruction or trapping a person.

Gate staff do not enter a moving lane to resolve a dispute or inspect a vehicle. An access problem is handled from a safe position. A collision, near miss or change that removes pedestrian separation is reported to the supervisor, and the affected movement is held while a safe arrangement is restored.

policies.title: Lone work and personal security
policies.description: Lone and remote work is arranged so a worker can obtain help without taking avoidable risks. This policy applies to isolated assignments, remote support and gate or security work.
policies.policyText:
# Lone work and personal security

Lone and remote work is arranged so a worker can obtain help without taking avoidable risks. This policy applies to isolated assignments, remote support and gate or security work.

The supervisor and worker consider the location, communication coverage, travel and likely hazards. They agree how to contact one another and how help will be summoned if contact is lost. The contact method and timing suit the work; Work needing a second person under an applicable safety rule is not assigned as lone work.

Workers keep a means of communication available and let the supervisor know when the work location or return arrangement changes. An aggressive person is handled by creating distance, using a safe exit and calling for assistance. Workers are not expected to physically confront an intruder or recover property at the expense of personal safety.

If contact fails, the responsible person uses the agreed response, including emergency services when the circumstances indicate danger. A worker who cannot obtain essential help pauses the exposed activity until communication or support is restored.

policies.title: Manual handling and ergonomic work
policies.description: Work is arranged to reduce strain, awkward posture and uncontrolled movement of loads. This policy applies to lifting, carrying, pushing, pulling and repetitive tasks.
policies.policyText:
# Manual handling and ergonomic work

Work is arranged to reduce strain, awkward posture and uncontrolled movement of loads. This policy applies to lifting, carrying, pushing, pulling and repetitive tasks.

Before moving a load, the worker considers its weight, shape, grip and route. Mechanical aids, smaller loads or assistance are used where needed to avoid losing control or excessive strain. The route is cleared and the destination prepared so a load does not have to be held while space is made. Hands are kept away from pinch points when setting material down.

Workstations and tools are adjusted to reduce prolonged reaching, twisting and force. Repetitive tasks can be varied or paused when the work allows, particularly when fatigue affects control. A worker does not attempt an unfamiliar heavy lift solely because another person previously moved the item.

Pain, tingling, weakness or a task that cannot be performed comfortably is raised with the supervisor so the method can be changed.

policies.title: Guards, tools and housekeeping
policies.description: Tools and machinery are used in a condition that protects people from cutting, crushing, entanglement and flying material. This policy applies to shops, maintenance work and field tools.
policies.policyText:
# Guards, tools and housekeeping

Tools and machinery are used in a condition that protects people from cutting, crushing, entanglement and flying material. This policy applies to shops, maintenance work and field tools.

Workers use the correct tool and compatible accessory for the task. Guards and safety devices remain in place during operation. Loose clothing, jewelry and hair are kept from rotating parts. Material is supported so hands do not enter a cutting or pinch zone. Tools with damaged handles, leads, guards or accessories are taken out of use until repaired or replaced.

Adjusting, clearing or servicing equipment is performed with hazardous energy controlled where the task exposes a person to unexpected movement. A jammed machine is not reached into while it can cycle. Compressed air, sharp scrap and cutting debris are handled without directing hazards toward other people.

Walkways, exits and access to controls remain clear. Spills and trip hazards are corrected or isolated promptly. A guard that interferes with the task is a reason to choose a suitable method or tool, not to bypass the guard.

policies.title: Specialist operations
policies.description: Specialist work is planned around its actual hazards and governing rules. This policy applies only when the company performs or supports radiation work, explosives operations, diving, marine work or rail activity.
policies.policyText:
# Specialist operations

Specialist work is planned around its actual hazards and governing rules. This policy applies only when the company performs or supports radiation work, explosives operations, diving, marine work or rail activity.

The manager identifies the specialist activity before assigning it. The people arranging the work establish which employer or operating authority controls the operation and how nearby workers will be kept clear. Equipment, access and communication are selected for the specific environment. Support staff receive the information needed to avoid entering the specialist work area or interfering with its controls.

Licenses, qualifications, medical provisions and operating arrangements are applied when the law governing that activity requires them. Radiation and explosives work use the relevant licensed arrangements; commercial diving follows its applicable diving standard; marine and rail activities follow the rules governing their location and operation. These duties are not assigned to companies that do not perform or encounter the activity.

An unexpected exposure, lost boundary or change beyond the planned activity prompts withdrawal and contact with the person directing the specialist operation. Untrained coworkers do not improvise a rescue or handle unfamiliar specialist equipment.

policies.title: Training matched to work roles
policies.description: Training is assigned according to the services a company provides and the tasks each person performs. This policy applies to company personnel, including new hires and people changing roles.
policies.policyText:
# Training matched to work roles

Training is assigned according to the services a company provides and the tasks each person performs. This policy applies to company personnel, including new hires and people changing roles.

The administrator selects the relevant positions and people on the course Policy page and sets the intended new-hire or role-change rule. Supervisors explain the duties of a changed role and identify training needed for hazards the person will encounter. A person performing one service is not assigned unrelated specialist training solely because it exists in the Library.

VNDRLY-required training follows the applicable service and role bundle. Additional vendor-selected training can support company work without becoming a scored VNDRLY requirement. Administrators use REVIEW to see who has or has not completed the relevant training, with available scores retained in the record.

Where a task has a legal qualification or evaluation requirement, the employer applies it to that task and role. Missing task training is addressed before the person performs work for which that training is required.

policies.title: Company and site orientation
policies.description: People receive understandable information about their work environment before exposure to unfamiliar hazards. This policy applies when joining the company, starting at a different site or taking on materially different duties.
policies.policyText:
# Company and site orientation

People receive understandable information about their work environment before exposure to unfamiliar hazards. This policy applies when joining the company, starting at a different site or taking on materially different duties.

The supervisor explains how to obtain help, report hazards, stop unsafe work and respond to an emergency. Orientation covers the person's actual work area, access routes, alarms, assembly arrangements and relevant restrictions. Site-specific information is obtained from the site contact rather than assumed from a previous location.

Instructions are provided in a language and form the worker can understand. The supervisor invites questions and checks understanding through conversation about the work. A worker can ask for an explanation without being treated as having failed a universal induction test.

Required role training is assigned through the applicable course policies. Changes in routes, alarms or responsibilities are communicated to the people affected. If a worker cannot identify the safe action for an immediate hazard, the supervisor resolves the uncertainty before assigning that exposure.

policies.title: Support for new and changed-role workers
policies.description: A person new to a task receives support appropriate to their experience and the hazards involved. This policy applies to new hires, transferred workers and experienced workers learning unfamiliar equipment or work methods.
policies.policyText:
# Support for new and changed-role workers

A person new to a task receives support appropriate to their experience and the hazards involved. This policy applies to new hires, transferred workers and experienced workers learning unfamiliar equipment or work methods.

The supervisor asks about relevant experience, explains the task and assigns work the person can safely perform. Instructions identify the hazards, safeguards and circumstances in which to stop and ask for help. An experienced coworker or supervisor remains available at a level suited to the task. Experience in one type of work is not assumed to cover a different machine or exposure.

As the person becomes familiar with the work, the supervisor adjusts support based on what the person can do safely. Questions and good-faith reports of uncertainty are encouraged.

When a task requires training, qualification or evaluation by law, that requirement is met before the person performs the regulated role. A mistake or unexpected condition prompts a safe pause, explanation and correction rather than pressure to continue beyond the person's capability.

policies.title: Training delivery and completion
policies.description: Company training gives workers usable instruction for the work they perform. This policy applies to courses assigned through VNDRLY and other training selected by the company.
policies.policyText:
# Training delivery and completion

Company training gives workers usable instruction for the work they perform. This policy applies to courses assigned through VNDRLY and other training selected by the company.

Training materials explain the subject, demonstrate decisions through examples and provide questions that check understanding. The administrator uses TRAINING to review the materials and ASSIGN to send a course to the intended people, groups or positions. Required new-hire and role-change assignments are configured on the course Policy page.

Learners answer the knowledge checks. When an answer is incorrect, the learner reviews the explanation and acknowledges the correct answer through the course's remediation process. Original and remediated scores remain distinct. Completion is recorded when the course's stated completion conditions are met. A separate certification exam retains its own passing standard.

The administrator uses REVIEW for company training compliance. Training completion contributes to the applicable training metric, alongside the other elements of the scoring rubric. A practical evaluation is required only for tasks where the governing law requires it;

policies.title: Commercial driving roles
policies.description: Commercial driving assignments match the driver, vehicle and service to the transport rules that govern them. This policy applies to regulated commercial motor vehicle operations.
policies.policyText:
# Commercial driving roles

Commercial driving assignments match the driver, vehicle and service to the transport rules that govern them. This policy applies to regulated commercial motor vehicle operations.

The person assigning a vehicle confirms the class of driving involved and uses a driver with the appropriate license and legally required endorsements. The driver follows applicable qualification, medical, hours-of-service and drug-and-alcohol program requirements where the operation triggers them. Those requirements are not imposed on employees who do not perform the regulated driving role.

Before travel, the driver considers vehicle condition, load, route, weather and available driving time. Loads are distributed and secured for the vehicle and cargo. Defects affecting safe operation are corrected before travel. Drivers maintain the inspection and duty records required for their operation.

The driver stops safely when fatigued, impaired or faced with an unsafe vehicle. The supervisor arranges a safe alternative rather than requiring the trip to continue. A change in vehicle class, cargo or service is checked for different legal requirements before assignment.

policies.title: Mobile equipment and lifting roles
policies.description: Equipment operators and people directing lifts receive preparation suited to the equipment and task. This policy applies to forklifts, mobile equipment, crane operators, riggers and signal persons within their assigned roles.
policies.policyText:
# Mobile equipment and lifting roles

Equipment operators and people directing lifts receive preparation suited to the equipment and task. This policy applies to forklifts, mobile equipment, crane operators, riggers and signal persons within their assigned roles.

The supervisor matches the operator's training and experience to the machine, attachments and work area. Operators understand capacity, stability, visibility and separation from pedestrians. They stop when the route or load cannot be controlled safely and report defects before another person uses the equipment.

Powered industrial truck operators covered by 29 CFR 1910.178 receive formal instruction, practical training and evaluation by a person with the required knowledge, training and experience. Their performance is evaluated at least every three years, with refresher training and evaluation when the standard's triggers occur. Construction crane operator certification, employer evaluation and signal-person qualification apply where the relevant construction crane rules require them.

These practical and qualification duties apply to the covered equipment roles, not every course participant or employee near equipment. A worker who has not been prepared for a different machine or lifting role tells the supervisor before undertaking that work.

policies.title: Permit, isolation, gas testing and electrical duties
policies.description: Safety-critical duties are allocated to people who understand the specific task and equipment. This policy applies to people issuing or receiving permits, applying isolations, testing atmospheres or performing electrical work.
policies.policyText:
# Permit, isolation, gas testing and electrical duties

Safety-critical duties are allocated to people who understand the specific task and equipment. This policy applies to people issuing or receiving permits, applying isolations, testing atmospheres or performing electrical work.

The supervisor explains the person's duties, limits and communication interfaces. A permit issuer understands the activity and conditions being authorized. An isolation worker identifies energy sources and verifies the controlled condition. A gas tester understands the detector, sampling location and limits of the result. An electrical worker performs only tasks within the person's electrical qualification.

Role training follows the governing task standard. Permit-space training, energy-control training and qualified electrical work practices apply where the corresponding regulations cover the work. A detector reading or a course completion is used for its actual purpose and is not treated as authority to undertake a different specialist role.

Workers do not accept a reading, permit or isolation they cannot verify within their duties. They ask the supervisor or responsible specialist to resolve the gap.

policies.title: First aid and emergency response roles
policies.description: Emergency coverage is arranged for the work location and the help that can reach it. This policy applies to occupational first aid and designated response duties.
policies.policyText:
# First aid and emergency response roles

Emergency coverage is arranged for the work location and the help that can reach it. This policy applies to occupational first aid and designated response duties.

The employer determines how workers will obtain prompt medical attention. Where an infirmary, clinic or hospital is not in near proximity, the first-aid training and supply provisions of the applicable OSHA medical and first-aid standard are met. Emergency contact information and the means to describe the work location are accessible to the people who may need them.

Designated responders receive the preparation required for their assigned response. Employees who only evacuate receive evacuation instructions rather than being assigned specialist firefighting, hazardous-material or rescue duties. Employees with occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious material are covered by the applicable bloodborne-pathogens protections.

At an emergency, workers raise the alarm, summon help and act within their training while avoiding further exposure. They do not enter an unsafe atmosphere or energized area to reach a casualty. After help arrives, the supervisor communicates relevant hazard information and protects private medical details.

policies.title: Equipment maintenance
policies.description: Equipment is kept in a condition suitable for the work it performs. This policy applies to company-owned, rented and hired equipment used in operations.
policies.policyText:
# Equipment maintenance

Equipment is kept in a condition suitable for the work it performs. This policy applies to company-owned, rented and hired equipment used in operations.

The person arranging equipment identifies the machine, its intended use and the operating limits supplied with it. Maintenance follows the manufacturer's instructions and any equipment-specific legal requirements. The supervisor arranges access to operating and maintenance information for the people who use or service the equipment. An asset list may help manage equipment, but

Operators report unusual noise, leakage, overheating, damage or a failed safety device. Equipment with a defect affecting safety is not used until the defect is corrected. Repairs are performed with hazardous energy controlled and with replacement parts suited to the equipment.

Before return to use, the person responsible for the repair confirms that the relevant guards and safety functions are restored. Statutory inspections and maintenance records are retained where the rule for the equipment requires them.

policies.title: Equipment checks and defects
policies.description: Equipment users check the conditions that can affect safe operation before use. This policy applies to tools, vehicles and equipment used in company work.
policies.policyText:
# Equipment checks and defects

Equipment users check the conditions that can affect safe operation before use. This policy applies to tools, vehicles and equipment used in company work.

The check is appropriate to the item: guards and leads on a power tool, visible damage and markings on lifting gear, or tires, controls and visibility on mobile equipment. A check is not a requirement to dismantle equipment or complete a generic checklist for every use. Equipment-specific legal examination and documentation requirements still apply where triggered.

If a defect could cause injury, the user stops using the item, keeps others from using it and informs the supervisor. Isolation, a tag, a barrier or removal from the work area can make its status clear, depending on the equipment. A warning label alone does not make a dangerous item safe to operate.

The supervisor arranges repair or replacement. The item returns to use after the defect has been corrected and the relevant safety functions checked. If the user cannot tell whether damage affects safe use, the equipment stays out of the affected operation while the question is resolved.

policies.title: Vehicles, trailers and loads
policies.description: Vehicles and trailers are used within their capacity and with loads controlled for travel. This policy applies to company transport, deliveries and towing.
policies.policyText:
# Vehicles, trailers and loads

Vehicles and trailers are used within their capacity and with loads controlled for travel. This policy applies to company transport, deliveries and towing.

The driver checks that the vehicle, hitch, trailer and load are compatible. Brakes, tires, lights and safety connections are in working condition. Cargo is distributed without overloading axles or defeating steering and braking, and is secured against movement. Doors, ramps and loose items are secured before the vehicle moves.

Loading areas keep people clear of vehicle movement and falling material. Drivers consider clearance, grade and road conditions when choosing a route. The operator does not move a load that obscures essential visibility or exceeds equipment limits. Regulated commercial transport follows its applicable inspection and cargo-securement rules.

For a breakdown or stuck vehicle, people move clear of traffic and tensioned recovery equipment. Recovery uses suitable attachment points and rated equipment; a tow ball or improvised connection is not used as a recovery anchor. If safe recovery cannot be arranged, the driver obtains appropriate assistance rather than exposing coworkers to a failed connection.

policies.title: Gas detection equipment
policies.description: Gas measurements use equipment suitable for the atmosphere and the decision being made. This policy applies to personal detectors and instruments used for atmospheric testing.
policies.policyText:
# Gas detection equipment

Gas measurements use equipment suitable for the atmosphere and the decision being made. This policy applies to personal detectors and instruments used for atmospheric testing.

The user confirms the gases measured, sensor range, alarm settings and limitations of the instrument. Readiness checks, functional testing and calibration follow the manufacturer's instructions and the requirements of the task. An instrument that cannot respond correctly, has a failed sensor or is outside its required calibration condition is not used to declare an atmosphere safe.

Sampling considers the location of people, possible gas layering, ventilation and the time needed for a remote sample to reach the sensor. Oxygen, flammability and toxic readings are interpreted for the instrument and hazard involved. A single clear reading does not establish that conditions cannot change.

An alarm prompts the worker to follow the escape or entry procedure for the task, not to silence the alarm and continue. Suspect results are checked from a safe position with suitable equipment.

policies.title: Pressure equipment and hose integrity
policies.description: Pressure equipment is selected, connected and maintained to contain its intended service. This policy applies to hoses, pipework, vessels, pumps and relief devices.
policies.policyText:
# Pressure equipment and hose integrity

Pressure equipment is selected, connected and maintained to contain its intended service. This policy applies to hoses, pipework, vessels, pumps and relief devices.

The person arranging the system confirms the working pressure, temperature, fluid and compatibility of components. Connections are made with the correct fittings and restraints for the arrangement. Hoses are protected from traffic, sharp edges, excessive bending and other damage. Relief devices are suited to the protected system and are not blocked or adjusted to overcome an operating problem.

Users look for wear, corrosion, leakage, damaged couplings and abnormal movement. Equipment with a defect affecting pressure integrity is removed from the affected service. A pressurized connection is not tightened, opened or repaired. Pressure is safely released and the isolated condition checked before maintenance.

If a hose fails or pressure control is lost, workers withdraw from the release path and the operator stops the supply where it can be done safely. Inspection and certification requirements apply to the equipment for which the governing rules require them;

policies.title: Lifting gear, access equipment and fall protection
policies.description: Equipment supporting a person or load is suitable for its purpose and kept free of defects that could cause failure. This policy applies to rigging, ladders, scaffolds and personal fall-protection equipment.
policies.policyText:
# Lifting gear, access equipment and fall protection

Equipment supporting a person or load is suitable for its purpose and kept free of defects that could cause failure. This policy applies to rigging, ladders, scaffolds and personal fall-protection equipment.

Users check the condition and identification relevant to the equipment before use. Slings and connectors are compatible with the load and attachment. Ladders have sound rails, rungs and feet and are placed to remain stable. Harnesses, lanyards and anchors form a compatible system with adequate clearance for the intended work.

Damaged equipment, items with unreadable capacity information needed for safe use, and fall-protection components subjected to an impact are taken out of use and handled according to the applicable standard and manufacturer instructions. Workers do not improvise repairs to load-bearing or life-support components.

Scaffold inspections, sling inspections and personal fall-protection inspections follow the rules for the actual equipment and work. A missing guardrail, damaged sling or unsuitable anchor is resolved before the person or load is exposed.

policies.title: Personal protective equipment
policies.description: Protective equipment is selected for the hazards that remain in the work. This policy applies to company tasks requiring eye, face, head, hand, foot, body, hearing or respiratory protection.
policies.policyText:
# Personal protective equipment

Protective equipment is selected for the hazards that remain in the work. This policy applies to company tasks requiring eye, face, head, hand, foot, body, hearing or respiratory protection.

The employer assesses workplace hazards and selects suitable protective equipment. Where 29 CFR 1910.132 applies, the hazard-assessment certification and employee training required by that standard are provided. Workers understand when protection is needed, how to put it on, its limitations and how to care for it. The equipment fits the worker and can be used with other protection without defeating either item.

Workers check their equipment and replace or report damaged items. Contaminated protection is handled so the hazard is not transferred to vehicles, eating areas or other people. Required equipment is available before the worker enters the exposure.

If protective equipment cannot be worn safely or does not control the exposure, the worker tells the supervisor and the task is adjusted. Respiratory protection, hearing conservation and other specialist programs apply when their own triggers are met.

policies.title: Safe shops and facilities
policies.description: Company premises provide safe access, usable emergency exits and work areas suited to their activities. This policy applies to shops, yards, stores and other company facilities.
policies.policyText:
# Safe shops and facilities

Company premises provide safe access, usable emergency exits and work areas suited to their activities. This policy applies to shops, yards, stores and other company facilities.

The person managing the area keeps walkways, exits, electrical panels and emergency equipment accessible. Materials are stored securely without unstable stacks or blocked routes. Lighting and ventilation are suitable for the work. Flammable materials and incompatible chemicals are stored under the requirements applicable to those substances.

Workers return tools and materials to safe locations, manage spills and scrap, and report damaged floors, exposed wiring or failed guards. Machinery is positioned so its operating space does not force people into traffic or moving parts. Charging, welding and similar activities are arranged so their ignition and ventilation hazards are controlled.

An immediate hazard is isolated or the affected area is closed while it is corrected. Fire and medical access remains available during deliveries and temporary work. Equipment-specific examinations and legally required fire provisions apply where relevant;

policies.title: Vacuum and high-pressure cleaning equipment
policies.description: Industrial cleaning equipment is operated to control pressure, suction, hazardous contents and movement of hose. This policy applies to vacuum trucks, hydroblasting and related cleaning systems.
policies.policyText:
# Vacuum and high-pressure cleaning equipment

Industrial cleaning equipment is operated to control pressure, suction, hazardous contents and movement of hose. This policy applies to vacuum trucks, hydroblasting and related cleaning systems.

The supervisor identifies the material being removed, the receiving capacity and any flammable, toxic or reactive hazard. Hoses, fittings and nozzles suit the pressure, vacuum and material. The crew controls hose movement and positions people away from the jet, suction opening and possible release paths. Deadman controls and other safety devices remain functional.

No one directs a pressure jet toward a person, reaches into a live suction line or clears a blockage with the system energized. The supply is stopped and pressure or vacuum safely released before opening or adjustment. Equipment is grounded or bonded where required for the actual flammable-material operation.

A leak, damaged hose or uncontrolled movement prompts an immediate safe stop. A suspected fluid-injection injury receives urgent medical attention even when the skin wound appears small. Tank or vessel entry follows the confined-space requirements triggered by that work;

policies.title: Reporting injuries and hazards
policies.description: Workers report injuries, illnesses, near misses and hazards promptly so people can receive help and dangerous conditions can be corrected. Reports can be made to the supervisor or another manager. Good-faith reporting does not result in retaliation.
policies.policyText:
# Reporting injuries and hazards

Workers report injuries, illnesses, near misses and hazards promptly so people can receive help and dangerous conditions can be corrected. Reports can be made to the supervisor or another manager. Good-faith reporting does not result in retaliation.

Immediate priorities are medical assistance and protection from further harm. The supervisor obtains the information needed to understand what happened without delaying treatment. Workers describe what they observed and distinguish facts from assumptions. A report can be made verbally;

The company makes government notifications required for the incident. Under federal OSHA's reporting rule, a work-related fatality is reported within eight hours, and a qualifying inpatient hospitalization, amputation or loss of an eye within twenty-four hours, subject to the rule's timing and reporting conditions. Applicable state reporting requirements are followed where they govern.

The responsible manager determines whether an OSHA recordkeeping entry is required and protects personal information. Near misses and ordinary hazard reports are not automatically treated as OSHA-recordable injuries. The affected workers are told how the immediate hazard has been addressed.

policies.title: Understanding incident causes
policies.description: The company examines incidents to understand what failed and prevent recurrence. This policy applies to injuries, significant near misses and other events selected for examination based on what happened.
policies.policyText:
# Understanding incident causes

The company examines incidents to understand what failed and prevent recurrence. This policy applies to injuries, significant near misses and other events selected for examination based on what happened.

Medical care and making the area safe come first. The supervisor gathers the relevant facts from the people, equipment and conditions involved. Questions address what the work required, what information and safeguards were available, and how the situation developed. Workers can explain their actions without being pressured to agree with an assumed cause.

The examination separates observations from conclusions. A person's last action is considered alongside equipment condition, task design, communication and competing work. The company chooses corrections that address the causes identified rather than relying only on a reminder to be careful.

The scope of the examination matches the event; Where a legally covered process incident triggers the investigation duties in OSHA process safety management, those specific duties apply. Relevant findings are shared with people whose work could be affected, with private information protected.

policies.title: Correcting unsafe conditions
policies.description: Unsafe conditions are corrected in a way that addresses the hazard people actually face. This policy applies to problems identified through work, reports, equipment faults and incidents.
policies.policyText:
# Correcting unsafe conditions

Unsafe conditions are corrected in a way that addresses the hazard people actually face. This policy applies to problems identified through work, reports, equipment faults and incidents.

The supervisor first protects anyone exposed. A permanent solution is selected with the people who understand the task. Removing the hazard or fixing equipment is preferred where practicable to adding warnings around a condition that can be eliminated. If a temporary measure is needed, the affected workers know how it protects them and where its limits are.

The person arranging the correction makes responsibility clear and follows up at a time appropriate to the risk. Work is not represented as safe merely because a task has been marked complete. Before affected work resumes, the crew confirms that the condition has been corrected or controlled for that work.

Workers report a correction that does not work or introduces a different hazard. The supervisor revises the solution rather than treating the first action as final.

policies.title: Sharing useful safety learning
policies.description: Safety learning is communicated to people whose work can benefit from it. This policy applies to lessons from incidents, near misses, changed equipment and successful improvements.
policies.policyText:
# Sharing useful safety learning

Safety learning is communicated to people whose work can benefit from it. This policy applies to lessons from incidents, near misses, changed equipment and successful improvements.

The supervisor shares the facts needed to recognize the hazard and use the improved work method. A useful message states what happened, the condition that mattered and the action relevant to the recipient's work. Personal medical information and unrelated identifying details are left out. An uncertain cause is described as uncertain rather than presented as an established fact.

Workers can ask how a lesson applies to their task and point out differences in equipment or conditions. A lesson from another operation is not automatically converted into a mandatory company rule. If it reveals an actual hazard in current work, the supervisor addresses that hazard with the affected crew.

A brief discussion after unusual work can identify what helped and what should change. Where the lesson changes an instruction people rely on, the current instruction is updated and explained to those affected.

policies.title: Accurate safety and exposure information
policies.description: Company safety information accurately represents the period, people and operations it describes. This policy applies to injury history, hours, exposure measurements and information supplied for safety reporting.
policies.policyText:
# Accurate safety and exposure information

Company safety information accurately represents the period, people and operations it describes. This policy applies to injury history, hours, exposure measurements and information supplied for safety reporting.

The person preparing information uses the underlying records and checks that totals refer to the same period and company scope. Estimates are identified as estimates. Missing information is not entered as zero, and a blank field is not described as proof that no incidents occurred. Corrections are made when an error is discovered rather than carried into a later report.

OSHA recordkeeping decisions use the applicable recording criteria and exemptions. An injury is not omitted to improve a rate or because a worker completed training. Exposure results identify the substance or hazard measured and the conditions represented by the sample; a result from one task is not assumed to cover every service.

Access to medical and personal information is limited to its legitimate use. Required records are kept for the periods set by the rule governing them.

policies.title: Medical help and return to work
policies.description: People receive prompt assistance after injury or illness, and medical information is handled privately. This policy applies to work-related medical response and arrangements for resuming work.
policies.policyText:
# Medical help and return to work

People receive prompt assistance after injury or illness, and medical information is handled privately. This policy applies to work-related medical response and arrangements for resuming work.

Workers call for emergency help when needed and notify the supervisor without delaying care. The supervisor provides responders with the location and relevant hazards, including chemical information when exposure is suspected. First aid is given within the responder's training while avoiding additional danger.

The company receives only the medical information needed for its lawful responsibilities, such as work restrictions or a legally required exposure-surveillance opinion. Detailed diagnoses are not circulated to coworkers. Access, disclosure and retention follow the rules governing the particular medical or exposure record.

When a person returns with restrictions, the supervisor arranges duties within those restrictions and seeks clarification when the job cannot be performed as described. Medical evaluations are obtained when the actual work or governing rule requires them. A worker experiencing worsening symptoms is helped to obtain care rather than pressured to complete an assignment.

policies.title: Emergency action and site coordination
policies.description: Workers know how to raise an alarm, leave danger and obtain help at their work location. This policy applies to emergencies affecting company personnel.
policies.policyText:
# Emergency action and site coordination

Workers know how to raise an alarm, leave danger and obtain help at their work location. This policy applies to emergencies affecting company personnel.

The person directing the work explains the alarm method, emergency contact, evacuation route and assembly location. At a shared site, the company uses the site's relevant emergency information and clarifies how its people will be accounted for. Routes and assembly locations avoid the hazard rather than simply following the shortest path.

On an alarm or discovery of an emergency, workers stop safely if time permits, warn others and move to the designated safe location. They tell the responsible person about missing coworkers or information responders need. They do not reenter the danger area to collect belongings or search without an appropriate response role.

Where 29 CFR 1910.38 requires an emergency action plan, the employer provides its required elements and employee review; the standard permits oral communication of the plan for employers with ten or fewer employees. Other applicable emergency rules are followed for their specific work.

policies.title: Rescue arrangements
policies.description: Work with a foreseeable need for assisted rescue is arranged so help can reach a person without exposing unprotected coworkers. This policy applies to confined-space entry, fall-arrest work and other tasks with a rescue hazard.
policies.policyText:
# Rescue arrangements

Work with a foreseeable need for assisted rescue is arranged so help can reach a person without exposing unprotected coworkers. This policy applies to confined-space entry, fall-arrest work and other tasks with a rescue hazard.

The supervisor considers how an incapacitated person could be reached and removed, the location's access and the equipment needed. Calling emergency services is considered in light of the response the task needs, rather than assumed to solve every rescue problem. Workers understand how to summon that help and keep the access route available.

For permit-space work, the employer meets the rescue-service evaluation, access and practice provisions of the applicable confined-space rule. For personal fall-arrest work, prompt rescue or self-rescue is provided as required by the governing fall-protection rule. These task-specific obligations are not imposed on staff without those exposures.

During an emergency, workers raise the alarm and keep clear of the hazard unless prepared and assigned to the rescue involved. A failed rescue arrangement is addressed before the exposed task continues.

policies.title: Emergency practice
policies.description: Emergency practice helps people use the response arrangements relevant to their work. This policy applies when the company practices an alarm, evacuation or specialist response.
policies.policyText:
# Emergency practice

Emergency practice helps people use the response arrangements relevant to their work. This policy applies when the company practices an alarm, evacuation or specialist response.
